title: Restriction, base change, and functoriality of Proj
statement:
Relative Proj has the following properties.

1. Its restriction to an affine open $V$ is canonically
$\operatorname{Proj}(\Gamma(V,\mathcal A))$, compatibly on iterated
restrictions.
1. A degree-preserving equivalence of graded algebras inducing the
chosen degree-zero base identification induces an isomorphism of Proj.
1. A surjective degree-preserving morphism of graded algebras induces
a closed immersion in the opposite direction on Proj.
1. If $g\colon X'\to X$ is flat, then coefficientwise pullback gives a
canonical base-change isomorphism
$$
\operatorname{Proj}_{X'}(g^*\mathcal A)
\cong X'\times_X\operatorname{Proj}_X(\mathcal A).
$$

The same base-change construction is required for an arbitrary morphism
$X'\to X$ when the universal blow-up lift is formed; that unrestricted
comparison is recorded as a separate conditional interface below.

proof.text: Write $P(\mathcal A)=\operatorname{Proj}_X(\mathcal A)$, with the structural map specified in [def-nagata-relative-proj]. By [lemma-nagata-relative-proj-exists], its inverse image of every affine open $V\subseteq X$ is canonically $\operatorname{Proj}(\Gamma(V,\mathcal A))$, and these identifications commute with further restriction and the structural maps. This is (1). In the remaining assertions work with quasi-coherent graded algebra sheaves on the specified base; their graded maps respect the base-algebra structures. Whenever two base affines overlap, compare their constructions on an affine refinement of the overlap, not by assuming their intersection affine.

Here are the affine-section facts needed below, including the sheaf-surjection issue. On $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$, [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] identifies a quasi-coherent module $\mathcal F$ with $\widetilde{\Gamma(V,\mathcal F)}$, naturally, and tilde preserves small colimits. Each homogeneous component of a quasi-coherent graded algebra is quasi-coherent: the degree projection is an idempotent $e_n$ on its underlying module, and its image is the cokernel of $1-e_n$; naturality of the counit and preservation of this cokernel identify it with the tilde of the corresponding module cokernel. Applying preservation of the coproduct indexed by $\mathbb N$ and then the unit isomorphism gives $\Gamma(V,\mathcal A)=\bigoplus_n\Gamma(V,\mathcal A_n)$, with the multiplication of [def-weil-pbc-graded-sheaf-structures]. If $\varphi:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ is surjective as a graded sheaf map, its degree-$n$ map is surjective (take the degree-$n$ component of a local lift). Put $u_n=\Gamma(V,\varphi_n)$. The counit identifies $\widetilde{u_n}$ with $\varphi_n|_V$. Hence $\widetilde{\operatorname{coker}u_n}=\operatorname{coker}(\varphi_n|_V)=0$, by preservation of cokernels. The unit isomorphism then gives $\operatorname{coker}u_n=0$. Thus the map on affine sections is surjective in each degree. No general exactness of sections on non-affine schemes is used.

For (2), let $\varphi:A\xrightarrow{\sim}B$ be the graded equivalence on an affine base, and $f\in A_d$, $d>0$. The fraction convention of [def-nagata-homogeneous-localization-degree-zero] gives $a/f^m\mapsto\varphi(a)/\varphi(f)^m$ on degree-zero chart rings. Applying $\varphi$ to a relation $f^k(f^n a-f^m b)=0$ preserves that relation, so the formula is well defined and is a ring homomorphism. Applying $\varphi^{-1}$ to fractions is its inverse. By spectrum functoriality in [def-weil-affine-spectrum], these ring isomorphisms give inverse scheme maps between the corresponding affine charts.

source.place: Tag 01MY (lemma-morphism-proj), fraction formula; Tag 01N0 (lemma-surjective-graded-rings-map-proj), specialization to an equivalence

proof.text: Use the standard-open identifications and covering of [prop-nagata-proj-standard-open]. For $f\in A_d$, $g\in A_e$ with $d,e>0$, [lem-weil-pbc-proj-basic-open-intersection] identifies the overlap inside the $f$ chart with $D(g^d/f^e)$. The chart homomorphism sends $g^d/f^e$ to $\varphi(g)^d/\varphi(f)^e$; after inverting these elements both chart formulas still send every fraction $a/t$ to $\varphi(a)/\varphi(t)$. They therefore agree under the transition equivalences of [lemma-nagata-proj-chart-ring-cocycle]. Glue the maps and, separately, the maps from $\varphi^{-1}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing]. Their composites restrict to identities on every chart, so uniqueness in that node makes the composites identities. On an affine refinement of any base overlap, restriction commutes with $\varphi$ and $\varphi^{-1}$, so the same fraction formulas agree with the restriction maps specified in [def-nagata-relative-proj]. Gluing once more over the base affines gives the asserted relative Proj isomorphism, respecting the chosen degree-zero base map.

source.place: Tags 01MY (lemma-morphism-proj), 01MZ (lemma-morphism-proj-transitive); scheme morphism gluing as in Tag 01LH (lemma-glue-schemes)

proof.text: For (3), fix an affine base and the resulting degreewise-surjective graded map $\varphi:A\to B$ from Step 2. Every homogeneous $b\in B_n$ has a homogeneous lift $a\in A_n$: alternatively take any lift in $A$ and then its degree-$n$ component. For $f\in A_d$, $d>0$, the fraction map $A_{(f),0}\to B_{(\varphi(f)),0}$ of Step 3 is therefore surjective: lift the numerator of $b/\varphi(f)^m$ in degree $md$. This is valid also for zero or nilpotent denominators; no cancellation is used. These elementary fraction arguments replace the two proposed localization lemmas.

The opens $D_+(\varphi(f))$, for all positive-degree homogeneous $f\in A$, cover $\operatorname{Proj}(B)$: lift every positive-degree homogeneous element of $B$ by Step 5 and apply [prop-nagata-proj-standard-open]. Glue their maps into the target charts $D_+(f)$ using the same overlap fraction computation as Step 4, [lemma-nagata-proj-chart-ring-cocycle] and [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing]. The inverse image of a target chart $D_+(g)$ is exactly $D_+(\varphi(g))$: on a source chart at $\varphi(f)$, with degrees $d=\deg f$, $e=\deg g$, the inverse image is the principal open of $\varphi(g)^d/\varphi(f)^e$, by [lem-weil-pbc-proj-basic-open-intersection] and the ring-map formula. Thus the restriction over every target standard affine is the spectrum of the surjection in Step 5, hence is a closed immersion by the affine criterion in [def-weil-closed-immersion]. This implies the global closed-immersion condition in that same definition directly: the image is closed because its intersection with each target chart is closed; the map is injective because two points with the same image lie over a common chart; the chart inverse homeomorphisms glue, and the structure-sheaf map is surjective locally, hence surjective as a sheaf map. Finally use [def-nagata-relative-proj] to identify affine base restrictions. The fraction formulas commute with restriction, so the maps glue over all base affines. The identical local closed-image, inverse-homeomorphism and sheaf-surjectivity argument then proves (3) for the relative schemes.

source.place: Tags 01N0 (lemma-surjective-graded-rings-map-proj), 07ZI (lemma-surjective-graded-rings-map-relative-proj); closed-immersion locality argument expanded from Morphisms Tag 01QO (lemma-closed-immersion)

proof.text: For (4), let $g:X'\to X$ be the given flat morphism and choose affine opens $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq X$, $W=\operatorname{Spec}S\subseteq g^{-1}V$. Put $A=\Gamma(V,\mathcal A)$ and $B=\Gamma(W,g^*\mathcal A)$. Each pulled-back component is quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-quasi-coherent]. Componentwise, [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-affine-sections] gives the isomorphism $\Gamma(V,\mathcal A_n)\otimes_R S\to\Gamma(W,g^*\mathcal A_n)$, $a\otimes s\mapsto s\,(g^*a)|_W$. Step 2 identifies sections of the underlying sheaf direct sums with the direct sums of these modules. The tensor direct-sum comparison is given by the mutually inverse maps induced by the inclusions and degree projections; each tensor involves finitely many homogeneous components. Swap factors by $s\otimes a\leftrightarrow a\otimes s$ to obtain a graded $S$-algebra isomorphism $\beta:S\otimes_R A\xrightarrow{\sim}B$, $s\otimes a\mapsto s\,(g^*a)|_W$. It is multiplicative and unital since pullback of the algebra structure in [def-weil-pbc-graded-sheaf-structures] gives $(s g^*a)(t g^*b)=st g^*(ab)$ and $g^*1=1$. Neither this comparison nor quasi-coherence requires flatness.

source.place: Tag 01I9 (lemma-widetilde-pullback), Tag 01IB (lemma-equivalence-quasi-coherent); pullback quasi-coherence as in Tag 01LA (section-quasi-coherent)

proof.text: Apply [lem-nagata-affine-proj-scalar-extension] to $R\to S$, $A$, $B$ and $\beta$. Its cartesian square, with the specified degree-zero structural maps, gives a canonical isomorphism $\operatorname{Proj}(B)\xrightarrow{\sim}W\times_V\operatorname{Proj}(A)$ by the uniqueness of an object with the fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product]. It also supplies the covering by the image denominators and the fraction formula for the map to $\operatorname{Proj}(A)$. In the chart at $f\in A_d$, the algebra isomorphism is exactly that of [lem-nagata-homogeneous-localization-scalar-extension], followed by $\beta$: $s\otimes(a/f^m)\mapsto s\,(g^*a)/(g^*f)^m$. With the tensor factors reversed this reads $(a/f^m)\otimes s\mapsto s\,(g^*a)/(g^*f)^m$. This corrects the factor-order ambiguity in the imported formula. Under the restriction identifications of [def-nagata-relative-proj], the target is the restriction to $W$ of $T=X'\times_X P(\mathcal A)$: maps to either fibre product are precisely pairs with the same map to $V$, since $W\to X$ factors through $V$. Thus we have inverse local isomorphisms between $P(g^*\mathcal A)|_W$ and $T|_W$.

Compare the local maps of Step 8 on base overlaps. At a point of $W_1\cap W_2$, choose an affine neighbourhood $V_0\subseteq V_1\cap V_2$ of its image and then an affine $W_0\subseteq W_1\cap W_2\cap g^{-1}V_0$, using [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. The restriction maps of [def-nagata-relative-proj] are the coefficientwise localized maps. Each of the two maps to $P(\mathcal A)$ on this refinement sends $a/f^m$ to $(g^*a)|_{W_0}/((g^*f)|_{W_0})^m$. On a further chart intersection, localizing the equality sends $u/v^k$ to the image of $u$ divided by the $k$th power of the image of $v$ in either order. Hence the maps agree on chart intersections under [lemma-nagata-proj-chart-ring-cocycle], not merely on generators before localization. They have the same structural map to $X'$, so the fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] makes their maps to $T$ equal. Glue these maps by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing]. Their local inverses agree because each is inverse to the same isomorphism on the overlap; glue those inverses as well. Both composites are the identity on the open cover indexed by $W$, and uniqueness of gluing proves they are the global identities. This proves the canonical isomorphism in (4). The argument actually works without flatness, but the statement is left unchanged; the separate arbitrary-base-change interface is not used here.

lean.note: The four clauses are supplied jointly by existing upstream declarations, not by the primary theorem alone. Basic supplies canonical affine restriction with naturality; Functoriality supplies the contravariant canonical map, its over-base equation, the isomorphism induced by a graded algebra isomorphism, and closed immersion for affine-section surjections; BaseChange supplies the canonical comparison and its fibre-product isomorphism for PullbackData (in particular for flat g). The homogeneous components are quasi-coherent, so sheaf surjectivity is equivalent to surjectivity on affine sections as detailed in proof Step 2. The added pullback-data definition node records the BaseChange module. All sources were read through scompile.py --source because the older local checkout lacks these modules.

blueprint_update.statement:
Relative Proj has the following properties.

1. Its restriction to an affine open $V$ is canonically
$\operatorname{Proj}(\Gamma(V,\mathcal A))$, compatibly on iterated
restrictions.
1. A degree-preserving equivalence of graded algebras inducing the
chosen degree-zero base identification induces an isomorphism of Proj.
1. A surjective degree-preserving morphism of graded algebras induces
a closed immersion in the opposite direction on Proj.
1. If $g\colon X'\to X$ is flat, then coefficientwise pullback gives a
canonical base-change isomorphism
$$
\operatorname{Proj}_{X'}(g^*\mathcal A)
\cong X'\times_X\operatorname{Proj}_X(\mathcal A).
$$

proof.text:
For (1), use the restriction isomorphism in
[lemma-nagata-relative-proj-exists]; transitivity of coefficientwise
localization gives the iterated-restriction equality. For (2), on an affine
chart the graded equivalence carries each homogeneous denominator to a
homogeneous denominator and induces an isomorphism of the corresponding
degree-zero localizations, hence an isomorphism of standard affine opens.
These maps agree on overlaps by the localization cocycle and glue uniquely.
For (3), a surjection has surjective maps on every homogeneous localization;
the induced maps on degree-zero rings give closed immersions of all standard
affine opens, which glue to the asserted closed immersion. Finally, for
(4), on $V=\operatorname{Spec}(A)\subseteq X$, put
$C=\Gamma(V,\mathcal A)$, and on
$V'=\operatorname{Spec}(B)\subseteq X'$ over $V$, the chart at a
homogeneous $f$ is identified on both sides using

$$
(C_{(f),0})\otimes_A B
\xrightarrow{\sim}(B\otimes_A C)_{(f\otimes1),0},
\qquad (x/f^m)\otimes b\longmapsto (x\otimes b)/(f\otimes1)^m .
$$

To justify this without a hidden cancellation argument, identify the
degree-zero homogeneous localization with the filtered colimit
$\varinjlim_m C_{md}$ whose transition map is multiplication by $f$.
Tensor product commutes with this filtered colimit, giving the displayed
isomorphism (in fact without using flatness). On pure fractions its inverse
sends $(x\otimes b)/(f\otimes1)^m$ to $(x/f^m)\otimes b$. It is compatible
with further localization, so the chart isomorphisms glue, and their
structural maps identify the glued schemes over $X$. This proves all four
assertions.
